application_manifest_cache.what: WinSxS\Manifests: the manifest of every component in the Windows component store.
application_manifest_cache.used_for: Windows servicing reads these to install, repair and update Windows. They are not rebuilt; only DISM/servicing may change them.
application_manifest_cache.risk: Deleting anything in WinSxS can leave Windows unable to boot or update. Microsoft says use Disk Cleanup or DISM /StartComponentCleanup instead.
application_manifest_cache.catalog_concern: Disabling is right. The disabled_reason text (whole app data folder / sign-in store) is the generic wording and does not describe this entry; the real reason is that it is system-critical.

browser_caches.what: The HTTP disk cache of the Default profile in Chrome and Edge (Default\Cache).
browser_caches.used_for: Pages and images are downloaded again as you browse; the folder is rebuilt automatically. Sign-ins, cookies and history are elsewhere and untouched.
browser_caches.risk: Pages load slower for a while. Files in use by a running browser stay behind.
browser_caches.catalog_concern: Description says Firefox but no Firefox path is listed, and only the Default profile is covered (Profile 1, 2... are not).

d3d_shader_cache.what: Compiled GPU shaders saved by DirectX (D3DSCache) and the NVIDIA/AMD drivers (DXCache, GLCache).
d3d_shader_cache.used_for: Games and apps compile shaders once and reuse them. After deletion each game recompiles them on its next launch.
d3d_shader_cache.risk: No data loss, but the first sessions of every game stutter or load slowly while shaders rebuild. Clearing it repeatedly (e.g. every Clean All Safe) makes that permanent.
d3d_shader_cache.before_cleaning: Close games and GPU-heavy apps first.
d3d_shader_cache.catalog_concern: Rated safe, so Clean All Safe wipes it every time and re-introduces shader stutter; caution fits better. Same paths as the other enabled shader entry (d3d_shader_cache / directx_shader_cache), so the same bytes are counted and offered twice; keep one.

defender_history.what: Microsoft Defender's detection history (Protection History) and scan result records under Scans\History.
defender_history.used_for: Windows Security shows these as past detections. Deleting them is an unsupported way to clear Protection History; Defender keeps working and writes new records.
defender_history.risk: You lose the record of what was detected and when (useful after an infection). Tamper Protection usually blocks the deletion anyway.
defender_history.before_cleaning: Clear history from Windows Security instead.
defender_history.catalog_concern: Catalog said safe; disabling was right. Disabled_reason wording is generic and inaccurate (not user data or sign-ins, but security evidence).

dev_tool_caches.what: Download caches of npm, pip, NuGet (incl. the global-packages folder), Cargo, Gradle, Maven and Yarn.
dev_tool_caches.used_for: Package managers reuse these instead of downloading again. After deletion the next build or install re-downloads everything it needs.
dev_tool_caches.risk: Large re-downloads; offline builds fail. Maven .m2\repository can also hold artifacts you built locally (mvn install) that exist nowhere else.
dev_tool_caches.catalog_concern: %USERPROFILE%\.nuget\packages and .m2\repository are package stores, not just caches; caution is correct but should say so. npm's own cache is %LOCALAPPDATA%\npm-cache.

diag_logs.what: Windows servicing and diagnostic logs: CBS, DISM, MoSetup, SIH, Windows Update ETLs, WDI traces, diagerr/diagwrn.
diag_logs.used_for: Only read when troubleshooting failed updates, SFC/DISM repairs or performance problems. Windows writes new ones; deleted history is not recreated.
diag_logs.risk: Lost evidence for diagnosing a failed update or corruption. CBS.log and active ETLs are locked while servicing runs.
diag_logs.before_cleaning: Only when no update or SFC/DISM is running and nothing needs diagnosing.
diag_logs.catalog_concern: Overlaps sfc_logs, windows_cbs_logs and telemetry (same files counted more than once).

directx_shader_cache.what: DirectX (D3DSCache) and NVIDIA/AMD/Intel driver shader caches, including AMD VulkanCache and Intel GLCache.
directx_shader_cache.used_for: Compiled shaders reused by games; rebuilt on the next launch of each game.
directx_shader_cache.risk: No data loss, but stutter and long first loads in every game until shaders are recompiled.
directx_shader_cache.catalog_concern: Rated safe, so every Clean All Safe re-introduces shader stutter. Same paths as the other enabled shader entry (d3d_shader_cache / directx_shader_cache), so the same bytes are counted and offered twice; keep one.

driver_store.what: The Driver Store: every driver package Windows has staged, including those for devices in use now.
driver_store.used_for: Windows installs and reinstalls drivers from here (new USB ports, repairs, updates). Not rebuilt if deleted.
driver_store.risk: Devices lose their drivers or cannot be reinstalled; can break boot. Remove superseded packages one by one with pnputil /delete-driver.
driver_store.before_cleaning: Never delete the folder; use pnputil.

dxgi_cache.what: Same GPU shader cache folders as directx_shader_cache.
dxgi_cache.used_for: See directx_shader_cache: shaders are recompiled by each game after deletion.
dxgi_cache.risk: Shader stutter after deletion; duplicate entry.
dxgi_cache.catalog_concern: Disabling as a duplicate is right.

event_logs.what: Windows event log files (.evtx): System, Application, Security and every operational log.
event_logs.used_for: Event Viewer, Reliability Monitor, auditing and troubleshooting read them. Logs are held open by the Event Log service; clear with wevtutil cl, not by deleting.
event_logs.risk: Destroys audit and troubleshooting history; clearing Security is treated as tampering (event 1102). Deleting the files under the running service can corrupt logs.
event_logs.before_cleaning: Never delete the files; use Event Viewer or wevtutil.
event_logs.catalog_concern: Catalog said caution; disabling was right. The disabled_reason wording is generic.

font_cache.what: FNTCACHE.DAT, the boot-time font cache kept by Windows.
font_cache.used_for: Speeds up font loading. Windows rebuilds it after a restart if it is deleted.
font_cache.risk: Slightly slower first boot; the file is locked while Windows runs, so deletion usually needs the Font Cache service stopped.
font_cache.before_cleaning: Stop the Windows Font Cache service; restart afterwards.
font_cache.catalog_concern: Small (a few MB); little to gain.

iis_logs.what: IIS web server request logs and HTTP.sys error logs (HTTPERR).
iis_logs.used_for: Used for web-site troubleshooting, traffic and security audits. Not recreated; IIS just writes new files.
iis_logs.risk: Lost web access/audit history, which servers often must keep for compliance or incident response.
iis_logs.catalog_concern: Rated safe but these are audit logs; caution fits. Current IIS logs default to %SystemDrive%\inetpub\logs\LogFiles, which is not listed.

installer_patch_cache.what: Windows Installer's $PatchCache$: baseline copies of files from MSI products, used when patching.
installer_patch_cache.used_for: Needed to repair, patch or uninstall patches of MSI software. Not rebuilt.
installer_patch_cache.risk: Future repairs and patch removals may demand the original installation media or fail.

language_packs.what: System32\MUI and System32\en-US: the language resource (.mui) files that hold Windows' own text and dialogs.
language_packs.used_for: Every Windows program loads its menus and messages from here. Not rebuilt; only a repair restores them.
language_packs.risk: Windows and its tools lose their UI text or fail to start. Remove language packs from Settings instead.
language_packs.catalog_concern: Catalog said caution; disabling was right (should be danger). The description 'cab files and MUI temp cache' is wrong: these are live system files.

memory_dumps.what: Kernel crash dumps: MEMORY.DMP, Minidump files and LiveKernelReports.
memory_dumps.used_for: Written after a blue screen or a live kernel hang; read with WinDbg to find the faulting driver. Not recreated.
memory_dumps.risk: The only evidence of a past crash is gone.
memory_dumps.before_cleaning: Only after the crash has been diagnosed.

minidump.what: %windir%\Minidump: one small dump per blue screen.
minidump.used_for: Holds the stop code, loaded drivers and stack of each crash, for diagnosis. Not recreated.
minidump.risk: Loss of the only record of past bugchecks.
minidump.catalog_concern: Same files as memory_dumps' Minidump path: counted twice.

ms_store_cache.what: Not documented by the vendor at this path. The Store keeps its cache in its package folder; wsreset.exe is the supported reset.
ms_store_cache.used_for: A Store cache would be rebuilt when the Store next opens.
ms_store_cache.risk: None known for a cache; the path may not exist on Windows 10/11.
ms_store_cache.catalog_concern: Path looks stale; prefer running wsreset.exe.

network_adapter_cache.what: The hosts file: manual name-to-address overrides (ad blocking, dev sites, blocked domains).
network_adapter_cache.used_for: Read by the DNS client on every lookup. It is configuration, not a cache; Windows does not recreate custom entries.
network_adapter_cache.risk: Lost custom entries: blocked sites reachable again, dev/intranet names stop resolving. DNS cache is flushed with ipconfig /flushdns instead.
network_adapter_cache.before_cleaning: Never delete; reset it per Microsoft's KB only if wanted.
network_adapter_cache.catalog_concern: Disabling is right; the description ('DNS and NetBIOS cached entries') is wrong.

notifications_cache.what: The notification database (wpndatabase.db): notification history and per-app notification settings.
notifications_cache.used_for: Action Center and app notification settings read it. Windows recreates an empty one, but app settings are reset.
notifications_cache.risk: Notification preferences and history are reset; the file is locked by the push notification service.
notifications_cache.before_cleaning: Only to fix a broken notification store.
notifications_cache.catalog_concern: Catalog said safe; disabling was right.

panther_logs.what: Windows Setup and upgrade logs (setupact.log, setuperr.log) in %windir%\Panther.
panther_logs.used_for: Read when diagnosing a failed upgrade or OOBE. Not recreated until the next setup.
panther_logs.before_cleaning: Only when no upgrade is in progress.
panther_logs.catalog_concern: Overlaps sysprep_logs and windows_setup_diags (whole Panther folder).

per_drive_found_clusters.what: FOUND.000 folders: file fragments (.chk) that CHKDSK recovered but could not reattach.
per_drive_found_clusters.used_for: Nothing uses them. Each .chk may hold a whole file, part of one, or junk.
per_drive_found_clusters.risk: Rarely, the only copy of something lost in a crash or power cut.
per_drive_found_clusters.before_cleaning: Look inside first if files went missing.

per_drive_recycle_bin.what: The Recycle Bin on every fixed drive: files you deleted.
per_drive_recycle_bin.used_for: Lets you restore deleted files. Emptying it deletes them permanently.
per_drive_recycle_bin.risk: Permanent loss of anything you might still want back.
per_drive_recycle_bin.catalog_concern: Correct, but the old hand-written scan_recycle_bin is still offered in the Large Items tab as safe.

per_drive_temp.what: A \temp or \tmp folder at the root of a fixed drive.
per_drive_temp.used_for: Created by a person or a tool on purpose; nothing in Windows manages it or recreates its contents.
per_drive_temp.risk: May hold files someone parked there deliberately.

photoscan_cache.what: The Photos app's LocalState: its library database, settings and (legacy Photos) Video Editor projects.
photoscan_cache.used_for: This is app data, not a cache; Photos would re-index, but projects and settings are lost.
photoscan_cache.risk: Lost albums/people tags, settings and video projects.

project_ascension_logs.what: Not documented by the vendor. Project Ascension launcher logs and its cache folder.
project_ascension_logs.used_for: Logs are only for troubleshooting; a cache folder is normally rebuilt by the launcher.
project_ascension_logs.risk: Lost launcher logs; launcher may re-download cached data.

sfc_logs.what: CBS.log and dism.log: the logs of SFC, DISM and Windows servicing.
sfc_logs.used_for: Read to see what SFC/DISM repaired or failed to repair. New ones are started; old content is lost.
sfc_logs.risk: Lost repair evidence; CBS.log is in use while servicing runs.
sfc_logs.before_cleaning: Not while SFC, DISM or an update is running.
sfc_logs.catalog_concern: Same files as diag_logs and windows_cbs_logs: counted more than once.

sysprep_logs.what: The whole %windir%\Panther folder plus CBS.log and setupapi.log.
sysprep_logs.used_for: Setup, Sysprep and upgrade diagnostics. Panther can also hold unattend files and migration data.
sysprep_logs.risk: Lost setup/upgrade evidence; deleting Panther during an upgrade breaks it.
sysprep_logs.before_cleaning: Only when no upgrade or Sysprep is in progress.
sysprep_logs.catalog_concern: Overlaps panther_logs, sfc_logs and windows_setup_diags. setupapi.log is the XP name; current files are INF\setupapi.dev.log / setupapi.app.log.

telemetry.what: Windows Error Reporting temp files, WDI diagnostic traces and diagerr/diagwrn logs.
telemetry.used_for: Diagnostics data that Windows rewrites as needed.
telemetry.risk: Lost diagnostic traces; pending error reports may not be sent.
telemetry.catalog_concern: Overlaps diag_logs. Deleting these files does not turn telemetry off.

temp_files.what: The user temp folder (%TEMP%) and Windows\Temp.
temp_files.used_for: Programs and installers put scratch files here. Most are leftovers; Windows does not need them after the program finishes.
temp_files.risk: An installer or app still running may need its files; the 24-hour floor protects most of these.

thumbnail_cache.what: Explorer's thumbnail and icon cache databases (thumbcache_*.db, iconcache_*.db).
thumbnail_cache.used_for: Previews of pictures, videos and icons. Rebuilt as you browse folders; your files are not touched.
thumbnail_cache.risk: Folders show generic icons until previews are rebuilt.
thumbnail_cache.before_cleaning: Locked by Explorer; some files only go after Explorer restarts.

thumbnail_cache_central.catalog_concern: Disabling as a duplicate is right.

update_cleanup.what: Windows Update downloads (SoftwareDistribution\Download, Backup) plus WinSxS\Temp and Windows\Temp\PostReboot.
update_cleanup.used_for: Downloads are fetched again when needed. WinSxS\Temp holds PendingRenames/PendingDeletes that servicing completes at the next restart.
update_cleanup.risk: Deleting WinSxS\Temp while an update waits for a restart can break that update. Download folder alone is fine with wuauserv stopped.
update_cleanup.before_cleaning: Stop wuauserv; never while an update is pending a restart.
update_cleanup.catalog_concern: Drop WinSxS\Temp (Microsoft: never delete inside WinSxS); Windows\Temp\PostReboot is also not documented. The SoftwareDistribution part is fine as caution.

update_orchestrator_logs.what: ETL trace logs of the Update Orchestrator (USOShared\Logs).
update_orchestrator_logs.used_for: Only read when diagnosing update scheduling. New traces are written.

user_crash_dumps.what: User-mode crash dumps written by Windows Error Reporting (%LOCALAPPDATA%\CrashDumps) and .dmp files in %TEMP%.
user_crash_dumps.used_for: Used by developers or support to diagnose an app crash. Not recreated.
user_crash_dumps.before_cleaning: Only after the crash is diagnosed.

wer_reports.what: Windows Error Reporting report folders: archived (sent) and queued (not yet sent) problem reports.
wer_reports.used_for: Reliability Monitor and support use them; queued reports wait to be sent to Microsoft.
wer_reports.risk: Lost problem history; queued reports are never sent.

windows_backup_catalog.what: Windows Server Backup logs in %windir%\Logs\WindowsServerBackup (not the backup catalog itself).
windows_backup_catalog.used_for: Read when a backup failed. Not recreated.
windows_backup_catalog.catalog_concern: Description says 'catalog and shadow copy history' but only logs are targeted. Same path as windows_backup_logs: counted twice.

windows_backup_logs.what: Windows Server Backup logs and the SIH (Service Initiated Healing) logs.
windows_backup_logs.catalog_concern: Overlaps windows_backup_catalog and diag_logs (SIH). SIH is servicing, not 'System Protection shadow copy logs'.

windows_cbs_logs.used_for: The record of Windows servicing and SFC repairs. Old content is not recreated.
windows_cbs_logs.risk: Lost evidence for update/corruption problems; CBS.log is locked by TrustedInstaller.
windows_cbs_logs.before_cleaning: Not while an update or SFC/DISM is running.
windows_cbs_logs.catalog_concern: Rated safe while sfc_logs/diag_logs rate the same files caution; caution is consistent. Counted multiple times.

windows_panther_logs.what: Not documented by the vendor. Panther\Tmp is a scratch folder of Windows Setup.
windows_panther_logs.risk: None known once setup has finished.
windows_panther_logs.before_cleaning: Only when no upgrade is in progress.

windows_setup_diags.what: SetupDiag/setup diagnostic logs plus the whole %windir%\Panther folder.
windows_setup_diags.used_for: Upgrade diagnostics; Panther may also hold migration data during an upgrade.
windows_setup_diags.risk: Lost upgrade evidence; breaks an upgrade in progress.
windows_setup_diags.before_cleaning: Only when no upgrade is in progress.
windows_setup_diags.catalog_concern: Overlaps panther_logs and sysprep_logs. The %LOCALAPPDATA% Setup\Diag path is not documented.

windows_tweaker_logs.used_for: Only for troubleshooting this tool. New logs are written each session.
windows_tweaker_logs.risk: Lost history of what the tool did (useful when reverting).

windowsupdate_orch_cache.what: SoftwareDistribution\Download and Backup: downloaded update packages.
windowsupdate_orch_cache.used_for: Windows Update downloads them again if still needed. Microsoft's reset procedure renames these folders with the services stopped.
windowsupdate_orch_cache.risk: Re-downloads; deleting during an install can make it fail.
windowsupdate_orch_cache.before_cleaning: Stop wuauserv and BITS; not during an update.
windowsupdate_orch_cache.catalog_concern: Description ('Orchestrator scan results') is wrong. Same paths as update_cleanup and wu_cache: counted up to three times.

winsat_cache.what: WinSAT (Windows System Assessment Tool) result files and log.
winsat_cache.used_for: Old performance scores; rerun 'winsat formal' to recreate them.
winsat_cache.risk: Scores read by some tools/games disappear until WinSAT runs again.

wu_cache.used_for: Packages are downloaded again if still needed.
wu_cache.risk: Re-downloads; an update being installed can fail.
wu_cache.before_cleaning: Stop wuauserv; not during an update.

wu_history_cache.catalog_concern: Disabling as a duplicate is right; the 'download history' wording is wrong (history is in DataStore, not here).

amd_shader_caches.what: Compiled shaders the AMD graphics driver stores per API: DxcCache (DirectX 12), DX9Cache, VkCache (Vulkan) and OglpCache (OpenGL). AMD Software's Reset Shader Cache deletes these stored shader cache files.
amd_shader_caches.used_for: Faster game loading and lower CPU use: AMD compiles frequently used game shaders once and reuses them on the next launch.
amd_shader_caches.risk: Games load slower and can stutter while the driver compiles the shaders again. No settings or saves are stored here.
amd_shader_caches.before_cleaning: Close all games. Clear it only to fix corrupted-shader glitches or to reclaim space; the AMD Software Reset Shader Cache button does the same.
